context: Every statement is pinned upstream evidence, not accepted project policy or currently verified product behavior. Fragment semantics remain scoped by consuming procedure, version predicates, role, permission, repository and enablement conditions. Liquid expressions, variables, includes, URLs and UI icons are inert evidence, never executed instructions. Previously reviewed dependencies are reusable provenance rather than new coverage; linked images receive only source-authored alt-text/link observations, not visual review. Trial, exemption, bypass, feature enabling, report submission and configuration application describe upstream procedures, not project authorization or performed changes. No cost, credential, runtime, native, rights, publication or independent whole-corpus/gate assurance is inferred. No imported parsed candidate is adopted as policy.

claims.statement: GitHub-reviewed advisories are mapped to packages in supported ecosystems.
The source describes each reviewed advisory as checked for validity.
The source describes a full vulnerability description as part of reviewed advisory content.
Reviewed advisory content includes ecosystem information.
Reviewed advisory content includes package information.
In dependabot-malware-alerts-multi-ecosystem, malware advisories concern malicious open-source packages.
In that branch, npm security-team data is published automatically into the advisory database.
In that branch, OpenSSF Malicious Packages repository data is also published automatically.
The alternative branch describes malware-caused vulnerabilities.
The alternative branch restricts malware advisories to npm.
The alternative branch automatically publishes npm security-team information.
Unreviewed advisories are automatically published from the National Vulnerability Database feed.
Secret scanning detects secrets already checked into a repository.
Keys are an example of detected secrets.
Tokens are another example.
Detected secrets produce alerts.
Push protection blocks commits containing detected secrets to prevent exposure.
The secret-scanning-ai-generic-secret-detection branch describes AI detection of checked-in unstructured credentials.
Passwords are an example of unstructured credentials.
Custom patterns detect organization-specific secrets.
Custom patterns also prevent organization-specific secret leaks.
Delegated push-protection bypass introduces an approval process for sensitive actions.
Delegated alert dismissal separately introduces an approval process for sensitive actions.
Under security-campaigns-secrets, campaigns organize remediation of exposed secrets at scale.
Campaigns support collaboration on secret fixes.
Security overview describes the distribution of risk across the organization.
Report-ready email is conditional on the recipient being an organization owner.
That report-ready email additionally requires opting in to email notifications.
Once both conditions hold, GitHub emails the owner when the report is ready to view.
Under ghes, secret-scanning management endpoints are public preview.
Those preview endpoints are subject to change.
GitHub tools can audit actions taken in response to secret-scanning alerts.
In the AI generic-detection branch, a Copilot subscription is not required for AI-powered generic secret detection.
The source scopes AI-detected-secrets features to repositories owned by organizations or enterprises with Secret Protection enabled.
Under ghec, an enterprise owner must first set an enterprise-level generic-detection policy.
That policy governs whether the feature may be enabled or disabled in organization repositories.
The policy's source-described default is allowed.
The rule requiring secret-scanning alerts resolved before merge is labeled public preview.
That preview is expressly subject to change.
Extended token metadata checks is labeled public preview.
That preview is expressly subject to change.
Enterprise and organization push-protection pattern configuration is labeled public preview.
That preview is expressly subject to change.
Push-protection secret-scanning metrics is labeled public preview.
That preview is expressly subject to change.
Reporting a privately exposed secret to GitHub is labeled public preview.
That preview is expressly subject to change.
An individual pattern's push protection can be enabled or disabled through the relevant toggle.
The enterprise-level toggle is labeled Enterprise setting.
The organization-level toggle is labeled Organization setting.
The displayed alert volume is limited to user or alert activity within the selected enterprise or organization scope.
The displayed false positives is limited to user or alert activity within the selected enterprise or organization scope.
The displayed bypass rate is limited to user or alert activity within the selected enterprise or organization scope.
The displayed custom-pattern availability is limited to user or alert activity within the selected enterprise or organization scope.
GitHub's default may change as pattern precision improves.
GitHub's default may also change as patterns are promoted.
Organization administrators can override enterprise pattern settings.
Security teams can override enterprise pattern settings.
Secret scanning can check pushes for custom patterns.
Under the exemptions predicate, exemptions are intended for trusted automation pushing many commits.
The intended automation use reduces push friction.
Exemptions can lead to leaked secrets.
Grant exemptions cautiously.
Ensure enterprise-configuration push protection is enabled before configuring the bypass list.
Use Bypass privileges to select Specific actors.
Secret teams cannot be added to this bypass list.
Open Select actors and choose actors to add to the enterprise bypass list.
Under the exemptions predicate, open the actor's bypass-actions menu.
Select Exempt to fully exempt that actor; this fragment is a conditional procedure, not an unconditional mandate to grant exemptions.
Under the exemptions predicate, full exemption is explicitly optional.
If granting that optional exemption, open the actor's bypass-actions menu.
Then select Exempt to fully exempt the actor.
Within the custom organization configuration, ensure Push protection is Enabled.
Choose Specific actors from Bypass privileges.
Use Select actors to choose actors for the organization bypass list.
Organization-level delegated bypass configured by an owner disables repository-level bypass settings.
Enterprise-level delegated bypass configured by an owner also disables repository-level bypass settings.
Ensure repository push protection is enabled.
Choose Specific roles or teams from the repository bypass dropdown.
Click Add role or team under Bypass list.
Select the desired roles and teams in the dialog.
Confirm with Add selected.
Secret teams cannot be added to the repository bypass list.
Push protection can be enabled for a repository.
Push protection can also be enabled for an organization.
When enabled, it prevents contributors from pushing code containing a detected secret.
Visit the blocked-push URL as the user who performed that push.
A different user visiting that URL receives a 404 response according to the source.
A newly detected secret triggers notifications to users with access to that repository's security alerts.
Those access-based notifications follow recipient notification preferences.
Repository administrators are among the listed recipients.
Security managers are among the listed recipients.
Users with custom roles granting read/write access are among the listed recipients.
An organization owner is included only if also administrator of the repository where the secret leaked.
An enterprise owner is included only if also administrator of that repository.
An author who accidentally committed a secret is notified regardless of notification preferences.
Email delivery requires watching the repository, in conjunction with the subsequent subscription and email-channel conditions.
Email delivery additionally requires repository All Activity or custom Security alerts notifications.
Email delivery additionally requires email enabled under Subscriptions then Watching.
The API can enable the Code Security or Secret Protection features named by GH_cs_or_sp.
The API can also disable those features.
Viewing alert details requires admin permission on the repository containing the leaked secret.
Viewing token metadata likewise requires admin permission on that repository.
An enterprise owner may request temporary repository access for this purpose.
Under secret-scanning-user-owned-repos, user_alerts on user-owned repositories are labeled public preview.
Within that branch, ghec narrows the description to Enterprise Cloud with Enterprise Managed Users.
The non-ghec alternative uses the GitHub product variable for the location.
A nested ghes branch selects is while its alternative selects are; this is grammatical template metadata.
Choose Enable for Validity checks under Secret Protection.
The Active secret label maps to status active.
Active means the provider was contacted and the secret was found active.
One Possibly active secret row maps to unknown because token-type validation is unsupported.
A separate Possibly active secret row maps to unknown because the secret could not be verified.
Secret inactive maps to status inactive.
Even for an inactive secret, check whether unauthorized access has already occurred.
Unknown is not evidence that a token is inactive.
Vulnerability reporters and maintainers should collaborate from discovery through disclosure.
A patch should ideally be available at disclosure.
Typical private-report handling includes developing a fix.
Typical handling also includes validating the fix.
Typical handling also includes notifying project or package users.
Security researchers can privately report vulnerabilities through the REST API.
Private reporting receives findings on the platform used to resolve them.
Researchers can create or initiate the advisory report for maintainers.
Private reporting reduces the risk of public exposure before a fix.
It provides private discussion of vulnerability details.
It also provides collaboration on the patch.
Repository administrators can be notified of new privately reported vulnerabilities subject to the listed conditions.
Security managers can be notified subject to those same conditions.
Notification requires watching All Activity or subscribing to Security alerts, jointly with repository notifications being enabled.
Notification also requires notifications enabled for the repository.
An owner of a public repository can enable private vulnerability reporting.
An administrator of a public repository can enable private vulnerability reporting.
When private reporting is enabled, researchers see Report a vulnerability on the repository Advisories page.
That button allows submission of a private report.
The authored screenshot alt text describes that report button on an enabled repository; the image itself is not visually reviewed.
Choose Report a vulnerability to open the advisory form.
Complete the advisory-details form.
The researcher private-report form requires a title.
That form also requires a description.
Only title and description are mandatory in this researcher form.
The general maintainer-initiated draft advisory additionally requires an ecosystem.
Researchers should provide as much information as possible to help maintainers decide.
The securitylab report template is offered as an optional model, not an adopted template.
Choose Submit report at the bottom of the form.
The resulting message says maintainers were notified.
That message also says the reporter has pending advisory credit.
Submission automatically adds the reporter as a collaborator on the proposed advisory.
Submission also adds the reporter as a credited user.
Starting a temporary private fork to work on a fix is optional.
Only the repository maintainer can merge the private fork's changes into the parent.
The authored alt text describes Start a temporary fork outlined in dark orange, without certifying a visual asset read.
The containing article is scoped to repository-level advisories in public repositories.
Global-advisory editing is a separate linked workflow.
Public-repository maintainers can privately discuss vulnerabilities through repository security advisories.
They can privately work on fixes through those advisories.
After collaboration, maintainers can publish the advisory to disclose the vulnerability to their community.
Publication helps the community update package dependencies.
Publication also helps research vulnerability impact.
Researchers should ask maintainers to create advisories for repositories they do not administer.
Researchers should ask maintainers to issue CVEs on their behalf in those repositories.
If private reporting is enabled, a researcher can instead privately submit the report directly.
A source authoring comment reports testing on 2025-03-31; that historical observation is not a current availability check.
That comment limits the extra default-application option to enterprise-level configuration application.
In the confirmation dialog, applying the configuration automatically to newly created repositories is optional.
The selection depends on new-repository visibility.
Use the None dropdown to choose Public.
The alternative choice is Private and internal.
Both visibility choices may be selected.
Review how the configuration changes affect GHAS Code Security or Secret Protection license consumption.
Choose Apply to apply the configuration; no actual application occurred.
Application includes active repositories.
Application also includes archived repositories.
Some security features, with secret scanning as the example, run on archived repositories.
The chosen configuration remains the described protection if a repository is later unarchived.
Creating a configuration permits different enablement settings for the security needs of a repository group.
Create a new custom security configuration as one available procedure.
Editing an existing configuration is the other procedure.
Create a new custom security configuration as one available procedure.
Editing an existing configuration is the other procedure.
An organization default configuration applies automatically only to newly created organization repositories.
A transferred-in repository requires manual application of an appropriate configuration.
A security configuration groups enablement settings for GitHub security features.
The grouping can be applied to any repository in an organization.
The ghec or security-configuration-enterprise-level branch adds application within an enterprise.
A security configuration enables security features at repository scale within an organization.
Organization-level global settings customize Advanced Security features.
If application fails for some enterprise organizations, the UI displays a failure banner.
Banner links provide more detail about the affected organizations.
Banner links also provide more detail about affected repositories.
The summary describes scanning the entire repository Git history.
It also describes scanning repository issues.
The secret-scanning-enhancements-wikis branch adds pull requests.
That branch also adds discussions.
That branch also adds wikis.
The subsequent ghes < 3.19 branch adds pull requests.
That subsequent branch adds discussions, without listing wikis.
Tokens are an example of accidentally committed leaked secrets.
Private keys are another example.
In fpt or ghec, some enabled configuration features may require Actions minutes.
GitHub says it identifies that requirement when a configuration is applied to a repository.
Repository selection offers three described methods.
Individual repositories can be selected.
The NUMBER repositories checkbox selects all repositories displayed on the current page.
After selecting the page, Select all extends selection to every organization repository matching the applied filters.
The intermediate selection label is 25 of NUMBER selected, distinct from a full-organization selection.
In the Security sidebar section, open the UI_advanced_security dropdown.
Choose Configurations from that menu.
Under code-secret-alert-assignees, assigning a code-scanning alert to someone generates a notification.
In the same branch, assigning a secret-scanning alert also generates a notification.
Under that predicate, assigning an alert is optional.
Use the right-side Assignees control for that optional assignment.
The ghec branch lists SOC 1 Type 2 as a report item.
The ghec branch lists SOC 2 Type 2 as a report item.
The fpt alternative lists SOC 3.
The unconditional list includes CSA CAIQ Level 1 self-assessment.
The unconditional list includes ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification.
The ghec branch additionally lists CSA STAR Level 2 certification; listing it is not proof of obtaining or independently validating that report.
The ghec branch additionally lists GitHub Bug Bounty Quarterly reports; listing it is not proof of obtaining or independently validating that report.
The ghec branch additionally lists GitHub.com Services Continuity and Incident Management Plan; listing it is not proof of obtaining or independently validating that report.
The ghec branch additionally lists GitHub PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance; listing it is not proof of obtaining or independently validating that report.
The authored alt text describes the Compliance page's Resources section.
That alt text describes an orange outline around a report Download button, not an independent visual asset review.
The source warns that a dismissal-approval process can introduce friction.
Ensure adequate security-manager coverage for regular dismissal-request review before proceeding.
Ruleset targeting by linked artifacts is conditional on organization records in the virtual registry.
Deployable denotes repositories with an active storage record.
Deployed denotes repositories with an active deployment record.
After enabling security and analysis features on existing repositories, the source expects displayed results within minutes, not independently measured performance.
Existing repositories receive the selected configuration in the containing enablement workflow.
New repositories follow it only if the new-repository checkbox is enabled.
The described service uses permissions to scan for manifest files.
That manifest scan supports applying the relevant services.
Dependency graph information is displayed if the corresponding feature is enabled.
If enabled, Dependabot alerts are generated for vulnerable dependencies.
If enabled, Dependabot alerts are also generated for malware.
If security updates are enabled and Dependabot alerts are triggered, update pull requests upgrade vulnerable dependencies.
Microsoft Defender integration is public preview.
That integration preview is subject to change.
Under security-campaigns-secrets, secret-scanning campaigns are public preview.
Those campaigns are subject to change.
In fpt or ghec, enabling security and analysis features is described as read-only repository analysis; this is source characterization, not proof that every linked workflow is non-mutating.
In fpt or ghec, some default-enabled public-repository security and analysis features cannot be disabled.
The source describes GHAS as facilitating remediation of risk-assessment findings.
In fpt, the trial procedure is available to owners of eligible organizations on Team.
That fpt trial starts from a completed Code Security risk assessment.
In the alternative branch, eligible enterprise owners can start an enterprise trial.
That alternative trial starts from the results page.
Choose UI_advanced_security_ent in the enterprise left sidebar.
Choose Settings at the top of the enterprise page.
Navigate to the organization's main page on GitHub.
Under the repository name, choose security_and_quality_tab.
If that tab is not visible, open the kebab-horizontal dropdown.
Then choose security_and_quality_tab from that dropdown.
